text:
maya (PM): Quick sync — we need a clear pipeline for SLA/contract-driven product asks. Sales/support keep escalating 'urgent' requests straight to product. How do we consistently triage so roadmap work isn't derailed?

olivia (Support): +1. Current flow: Zendesk -> tags -> manual triage. For SLA accounts we add `sla_customer` tag and create a Jira when it's Sev1/2, but a lot of feature asks come through as 'urgent' with no context.

sanjeev (SRE): From SRE side: we need a severity -> routing map. Proposal: Sev1 (service down / major SLA breach) -> page SRE + account PM, create incident. Sev2 (major latency or partial degradation) -> page oncall + notify product owners. Use PD escalation policy `SLA-High`.

liz (Sales): Contracts vary a lot. Some customers pay for 24x7 support and 99.95% uptime. When we close deals we should auto-tag the account in CRM with SLA tier so support intake knows the response obligation. If it's a paid SLA, response timelines are contractual.

jack (Eng Lead): Important callout — we can't treat product changes as incident triage work. Need clear guardrails: when does something become a product priority vs an operational mitigation? We need acceptance criteria, a rollback plan, and an engineering estimate before we schedule product work.

maya (PM): Suggested triage matrix (short): 
- Impact: customers affected / revenue / compliance
- Severity: downtime / latency / degraded functionality
- Workaround: yes / no
- Effort: S / M / L
Score = weighted sum -> priority band. If score >= threshold -> label `sla-urgent` and route to SLA lane.

olivia (Support): We can extend the intake form to capture SLA tier, contract link, and auto-calc the triage score. If `sla-urgent` then auto-create Jira with label + include contract excerpt. That should help product triage quickly.

sanjeev (SRE): Routing rules idea: 
- Sev1: PD -> SRE -> immediate mitigation + page PM/account lead -> create incident ticket -> if needs product fix, attach hotfix request and tag `sla-urgent`
- Sev2: PD -> oncall -> mitigation, create ticket, notify product owners; product can decide to triage into backlog based on matrix
If product work is required for compliance, escalate to product with 48h commitment window.

liz (Sales): Also need to ensure legal/compliance flags (e.g., data residency) are surfaced. For Private deployments, SLA expectations differ. Include a field `deployment_type` in the intake.

ops-bot: ops-bot: created ticket PROD-SLA-4823 via support intake (https://jira.internal/PROD-SLA-4823).

jack (Eng Lead): Let's pilot this for our top 10 SLA accounts for 6 weeks. I'll prepare runbook templates and a minimal PRD for the escalation flow. We should also measure mean time to mitigation and time to product fix.

maya (PM): Launch criteria for moving an intake into product backlog (proposal): 1) triage score >= threshold; 2) PM sign-off (business sponsor noted); 3) engineering estimate attached; 4) security/compliance review if applicable. Otherwise it stays in ops backlog for mitigations.

olivia (Support): I'll update the intake form and add auto-tagging logic (CRM -> support tags -> intake). Also will include 'contract response SLA' field.

sanjeev (SRE): We'll add a PD escalation policy `SLA-High` and an oncall rotation that includes an SRE + product on-call notify. Add runbooks for common latency mitigations.

maya (PM): I'll draft the PRD for triage + escalation routing and share here by EOW. Will include the triage matrix weights and the product acceptance checklist. Can folks review when I post? :thumbsup:

liz (Sales): Yes — I'll attach a sample contract template so intake can parse response windows automatically.

jack (Eng Lead): One more: require a 'short-term mitigation plan' field on tickets so SRE can act without waiting for product decisions. That reduces risk of SLA breaches.

maya (PM): Great. Action items: 
1) olivia: modify intake form & auto-tagging (CRM integration)
2) sanjeev: PD escalation policy + runbooks
3) jack: runbook templates + engineering acceptance checklist
4) liz: sample contract snippets for parsing
5) maya: PRD draft + pilot plan for top 10 accounts

maya (PM): Thanks — will post the PRD here and schedule a 30min sync next week to align on implementation.
